title: Banach Gaussian priors, RKHS support, and concentration

items.title: Centered Borel Gaussian random element on a separable Banach space
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ be a probability space and let $B$ be a real
separable Banach space with its norm Borel sigma-algebra. A map
$W:\Omega\to B$ is a **centered Borel Gaussian random element** if it is
Borel-measurable and, for every $\ell\in B^*$, the real random variable
$\ell(W)$ has a centered (possibly zero-variance) normal law. Its law is the
Borel probability $\mu=P\circ W^{-1}$. When the word *tight* is used, it means
that for every $\delta>0$ there is a norm-compact $K\subseteq B$ with
$\mu(K)>1-\delta$.

This definition concerns a random element in $B$. A Gaussian process on an
arbitrary index set with only a cylinder-space law does not satisfy it unless
a Borel $B$-valued realization is separately constructed.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors (2008)
references.locator: Section 2.1, printed pp. 1436–1437: definition of a Borel Gaussian random element in a Banach space.

references.title: M. Hairer, An Introduction to Stochastic PDEs
references.locator: Section 4.2: Gaussian measures on a separable Banach space.

items.title: A Borel map into a separable Banach space is strongly measurable
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ be a probability space, let $B$ be a separable
Banach space, and let $f:\Omega\to B$ be Borel-measurable. Then $f$ is strongly
measurable: outside a $P$-null set it is the pointwise limit of finite-valued
measurable simple functions.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Section 2.3, measurable and strongly measurable Banach-valued maps.

items.title: A separable Banach space has a countable norming family
items.statement:
Assume HB and countable choice. Let $B$ be a real separable Banach space. There is a sequence
$(\ell_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq B^*$ with $\|\ell_j\|=1$ such that
$$\|x\|=\sup_{j\ge1}|\ell_j(x)|\qquad(x\in B).$$
If $B=\{0\}$, the conclusion is interpreted using the zero functional and the
supremum is $0$.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Section 3.1: separability and countable norming sets for Gaussian measures.

items.title: Finite-dimensional Gaussian isoperimetric expansion
items.statement:
Assume AC. For $d\ge1$, let $\gamma_d$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^d$,
let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be Borel, and let
$A+rB_2^d=\{a+ru:a\in A,\ |u|\le1\}$. Then for every $r\ge0$,
$$\gamma_{d,*}(A+rB_2^d)\ge \Phi\!\left(\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_d(A))+r\right),$$
where $\gamma_{d,*}(S)=\sup\{\gamma_d(K):K\subseteq S,\ K\text{ compact}\}$ is Gaussian inner measure, and $\Phi^{-1}(0)=-\infty$, $\Phi^{-1}(1)=+\infty$.

references.title: S. G. Bobkov, An isoperimetric inequality on the discrete cube, and an elementary proof of the isoperimetric inequality in Gauss space (1997)
references.locator: The Gaussian isoperimetric inequality and proof from the discrete-cube inequality, pp. 1–8.

references.title: C. Borell, The Brunn–Minkowski inequality in Gauss space (1975)
references.locator: Section 3, Theorem 3.1 proof, especially the finite-dimensional reduction on pp. 209–210.

references.title: D. Chafaï and J. Lehec, Lectures on the logarithmic Sobolev inequality, Chapter 4, Theorem 4.6, pp. 45–50
references.locator: Full PDF retrieved; complete semigroup proof pp. 49–50 read; the finite-ball neighborhood passage is supplied locally below.

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed as in the Gaussian suppliers; it implies DC and Countable Choice for the stated integration interfaces. The sharp inequality is proved locally by explicit Gaussian-semigroup calculus, smooth cutoffs and finite-ball approximation.

items.title: Gross logarithmic Sobolev inequality for standard Gaussian measure
items.statement:
Assume AC, DC, and countable choice, and let $\gamma_d$ be standard Gaussian
measure on $\mathbb R^d$. For every
$g\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$ bounded above and below by positive constants, with
bounded first and second derivatives,
$$\operatorname{Ent}_{\gamma_d}(g) :=\int g\log g\,d\gamma_d -\left(\int g\,d\gamma_d\right)\log\left(\int g\,d\gamma_d\right) \le \frac12\int\frac{|\nabla g|^2}{g}\,d\gamma_d.$$

references.title: N. Berestycki and R. Nickl, Concentration of Measure
references.locator: Chapter 4, Theorem 11 and complete proof: Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality.

references.title: D. Chafaï and D. Lehec, Lectures on the logarithmic Sobolev inequality
references.locator: Gaussian Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup proof of the logarithmic Sobolev inequality.

items.title: A countable norming family determines Borel laws
items.statement: Let $B$ be a separable Banach space, and let $(\ell_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq B^*$ satisfy the norming identity $\|x\|=\sup_{j\ge1}|\ell_j(x)|$ for every $x\in B$. If Borel probabilities $\mu,\nu$ on $B$ have equal finite-dimensional pushforwards under every finite subfamily of $(\ell_j)$, then $\mu=\nu$.

references.title: M. Hairer, An Introduction to Stochastic PDEs
references.locator: Proposition 4.11: a countable separating family determines the Borel Gaussian law.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Sections 2.1 and 3.1: Borel sigma-algebras and Gaussian measures on separable Banach spaces.

items.title: Lipschitz concentration for standard Gaussian measure
items.statement:
Assume AC, DC, and countable choice. Let $Z\sim\gamma_d$ be standard Gaussian
on $\mathbb R^d$ and let
$f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be $L$-Lipschitz. If $L>0$, then for every $r>0$,
$$P\{f(Z)\ge E f(Z)+r\}\le e^{-r^2/(2L^2)}.$$
If $L=0$, the probability on the left is zero.

references.title: N. Berestycki and R. Nickl, Concentration of Measure
references.locator: Chapter 4, Theorem 9 and the Herbst argument, followed by Theorem 10.

references.title: D. Chafaï and D. Lehec, Lectures on the logarithmic Sobolev inequality
references.locator: Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality and Herbst concentration argument.

items.title: Uncorrelated jointly Gaussian Banach random elements are independent
items.statement:
Assume AC and countable choice. Let $X$ and $Y$ be jointly centered Gaussian Borel random elements taking
values in real separable Banach spaces $B_1$ and $B_2$. Here jointly Gaussian
means every finite family of continuous linear coordinates of $(X,Y)$ has a
multivariate normal law. If
$E[\ell(X)m(Y)]=0$ for every $\ell\in B_1^*$ and $m\in B_2^*$, then $X$ and
$Y$ are independent.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Section 3.1: Gaussian orthogonality, independence, and countable determining families.

references.title: M. Hairer, An Introduction to Stochastic PDEs
references.locator: Section 4.2: independence of Gaussian components.

items.title: Fernique integrability for a separable Banach Gaussian law
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $W$ be a centered Borel Gaussian random
element in a real separable Banach space $B$. There is a constant $a>0$ such
that
$$E\exp(a\|W\|^2)<\infty.$$
In particular, $E\|W\|^2<\infty$.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Theorem 2.3.1 and complete proof, source PDF pp. 25–26.

references.title: M. Hairer, An Introduction to Stochastic PDEs
references.locator: Theorem 4.13 and complete proof, source PDF pp. 20–21.

items.title: Covariance operator and reproducing-kernel Hilbert space of a Banach Gaussian
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $W$ be a centered Borel Gaussian random element in a real separable
Banach space $B$, with law $\mu$. For $\ell\in B^*$ define
$$C\ell=E[\ell(W)W]\in B,\qquad Q(\ell,m)=E[\ell(W)m(W)]\quad(\ell,m\in B^*).$$
The **Cameron–Martin reproducing-kernel Hilbert space** $H$ is the completion
of $B^*/N$ in the inner product induced by $Q$, where
$N=\{\ell\in B^*:Q(\ell,\ell)=0\}$. The canonical map sends the class of
$\ell$ to $C\ell$ and extends continuously to an injective map $i:H\to B$;
we identify $H$ with its image in $B$ and use the completed Hilbert norm
$\|\cdot\|_H$. The preceding construction is well-defined by
[[thm-banach-gaussian-covariance-rkhs-is-well-defined]].

The term *RKHS* here denotes this covariance-induced Hilbert space of shifts
inside $B$; it is not the space of all continuous functions on an arbitrary
index set.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors (2008)
references.locator: Section 2.1, printed pp. 1436–1437: covariance operator and RKHS construction.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Section 3.1: covariance operator, Cameron–Martin space, and its canonical embedding.

items.title: Borell concentration for the norm of a separable Banach Gaussian
items.statement:
Assume AC, DC, and countable choice. Let $W$ be a centered Borel Gaussian
random element in a real separable
Banach space $B$. Define
$$\sigma^2=\sup_{\|\ell\|_{B^*}\le1}E[\ell(W)^2].$$
For $r\ge0$, if $\sigma>0$ then
$$P\{\|W\|>E\|W\|+r\}\le e^{-r^2/(2\sigma^2)}.$$
If $\sigma=0$, then $W=0$ almost surely and the tail probability is zero.

references.title: N. Berestycki and R. Nickl, Concentration of Measure
references.locator: Chapter 4, Theorem 10 and complete proof; §4.4 for Banach-valued Gaussian norm concentration.

references.title: C. Borell, The Brunn–Minkowski inequality in Gauss space (1975)
references.locator: Section 5, Theorems 5.1–5.2: tails of measurable Gaussian seminorms.

items.title: The Banach Gaussian covariance and RKHS construction is well-defined
items.statement:
Assume AC. Under the hypotheses and notation of
[[def-banach-gaussian-covariance-operator-and-rkhs]], each $C\ell$ exists as a
Bochner integral; $Q$ is a finite positive-semidefinite bilinear form;
$N=\{\ell:Q(\ell,\ell)=0\}$ is its nullspace; and the induced map from the
completion of $B^*/N$ to $B$ is continuous and injective. Thus the definition
identifies a Hilbert space of shifts in $B$.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors (2008)
references.locator: Section 2.1, printed pp. 1436–1437: covariance operator and quotient RKHS construction.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Section 3.1: covariance bilinear form and canonical embedding of the completed RKHS.

items.title: Cameron–Martin translation formula for a separable Banach Gaussian
items.statement:
Assume AC and countable choice. Let $W$ be a centered Borel Gaussian random
element in a real separable
Banach space $B$, with law $\mu$ and covariance RKHS $H\subseteq B$. For
$h\in H$, let $z_h$ be the $L^2(\mu)$-limit of the coordinate functions
$\ell(x)$ representing a sequence of classes $[\ell]\to i^{-1}h$ in the
completion $H$. The limit has a $\mu$-measurable version and does not depend
on the approximating sequence. If $\mu_h$ denotes the law of $W+h$, then
$$\frac{d\mu_h}{d\mu}(x) =\exp\!\left(z_h(x)-\frac12\|h\|_H^2\right).$$
In particular, $\mu_h$ and $\mu$ are equivalent. If $h=C\ell$ for
$\ell\in B^*$, then $z_h(x)=\ell(x)$ $\mu$-almost surely and
$\|h\|_H^2=E[\ell(W)^2]$; these formulas are independent of the choice of
representative $\ell$.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Theorem 3.1.5 and complete proof, source PDF pp. 34–36.

references.title: M. Hairer, An Introduction to Stochastic PDEs
references.locator: Theorem 4.44 and proof, Cameron–Martin translation formula.

items.title: The Cameron–Martin unit ball is compact in the Banach norm
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $\mu$ be a centered tight Borel Gaussian law on a real separable Banach
space $B$, and let $H\subset B$ be its covariance RKHS. The closed Hilbert
unit ball
$$H_1=\{h\in H:\|h\|_H\le1\}$$
is compact in the Banach norm.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Theorem 3.1.9 and complete proof, source PDF pp. 38–39.

references.title: M. Hairer, An Introduction to Stochastic PDEs
references.locator: Section 4.2: compactness of the Cameron–Martin unit ball.

items.title: The support of a Banach Gaussian is the closure of its RKHS
items.statement:
Assume AC and countable choice. Let $\mu$ be a centered tight Borel Gaussian
law on a real separable Banach
space $B$, and let $H\subseteq B$ be its covariance RKHS. Define
$\operatorname{supp}\mu$ to be the set of $x\in B$ for which every open
neighborhood has positive $\mu$-measure. Then
$$\operatorname{supp}\mu=\overline H^{\,B}.$$

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors (2008)
references.locator: Section 2.1, printed pp. 1436–1438: support of a Borel Gaussian law.

references.title: M. Hairer, An Introduction to Stochastic PDEs
references.locator: Exercise 4.46 and surrounding discussion, source PDF pp. 25–26.

items.title: Concentration function of a Banach Gaussian prior
items.statement:
Assume AC and countable choice. Let $\mu$ be a centered tight Borel Gaussian law on a real separable Banach
space $B$, with covariance RKHS $H$, and let $w_0\in\overline H^{\,B}$. For
$\varepsilon>0$, write
$\varepsilon B^\circ=\{x\in B:\|x\|_B<\varepsilon\}$ and define the
**concentration function**
$$\phi_{w_0}(\varepsilon) =\inf_{\substack{h\in H\\\|h-w_0\|_B<\varepsilon}} \left\{\|h\|_H^2-\log\mu(\varepsilon B^\circ)\right\}.$$
The feasible set is nonempty because $w_0$ lies in the Banach-norm closure of
$H$. Also $\mu(\varepsilon B^\circ)>0$ because $0\in\operatorname{supp}\mu$;
thus the logarithm is finite. The value is finite and nonnegative. The support assertion used here is
[[thm-support-of-banach-gaussian-is-closure-of-rkhs]].

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors (2008)
references.locator: Section 2.1, printed p. 1437: definition of the concentration function.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Section 3.1: Cameron–Martin norm and small-ball probabilities.

items.title: Borell–Sudakov–Tsirelson expansion for a Banach Gaussian law
items.statement:
Assume AC and countable choice. Let $\mu$ be a centered tight Borel Gaussian law on a real separable Banach
space $B$, with covariance RKHS $H$ and unit ball $H_1$. For every Borel set
$A\subseteq B$ and $r\ge0$,
$$\mu_*(A+rH_1)\ge \Phi\!\left(\Phi^{-1}(\mu(A))+r\right),$$
where $\mu_*(S)=\sup\{\mu(K):K\subseteq S,\ K\text{ compact}\}$ is the inner
measure and $\Phi^{-1}(0)=-\infty$, $\Phi^{-1}(1)=+\infty$. When
$A+rH_1$ is Borel, its inner measure equals its ordinary $\mu$-measure.

references.title: C. Borell, The Brunn–Minkowski inequality in Gauss space (1975)
references.locator: Section 3, Theorem 3.1 and complete two-step proof, printed pp. 208–210.

references.title: M. Hairer, An Introduction to Stochastic PDEs
references.locator: Theorem 4.53 and the surrounding reduction to Gaussian isoperimetry; the source explicitly omits its proof.

items.axiom_use: AC supplies HB for the point-separation step, while countable choice supplies the countable subcover. The finite-dimensional sharp expansion is proved by its local Gaussian-semigroup and finite-ball argument.

items.title: Gaussian concentration-function sieve bounds
items.statement:
Assume AC and countable choice. Let $\mu$ be a centered tight Borel Gaussian
law on a real separable Banach
space $B$, with covariance RKHS $H$, and let $w_0\in\overline H^{\,B}$.
Suppose $n\ge1$, $\varepsilon>0$, $C>1$,
$e^{-Cn\varepsilon^2}<1/2$, and
$\phi_{w_0}(\varepsilon)\le n\varepsilon^2$, where $\phi_{w_0}$ is the
concentration function. Then there is a measurable set $B_n\subseteq B$
such that
$$\log N(3\varepsilon,B_n,\|\cdot\|_B)\le6Cn\varepsilon^2,\qquad \mu(B\setminus B_n)\le e^{-Cn\varepsilon^2},$$
and
$$\mu\{\|W-w_0\|_B<2\varepsilon\}\ge e^{-n\varepsilon^2}.$$
These are prior-mass and sieve bounds only; they assert no posterior
contraction without separate statistical-distance and Kullback–Leibler
comparisons.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors (2008)
references.locator: Theorem 2.1 and complete proof in §5, printed pp. 1437–1440 and 1454–1456.

references.title: C. Borell, The Brunn–Minkowski inequality in Gauss space (1975)
references.locator: Section 3, Theorem 3.1: Gaussian enlargement inequality used for the sieve tail.

items.axiom_use: The result uses the declared Gaussian, Cameron–Martin, inner-regularity and expansion interfaces. AC supplies HB for the norming coordinates; no statistical-model or posterior-contraction assumption is made.

title: Banach Gaussian priors, RKHS support, and concentration — Examples

items.title: An iid Gaussian cylinder process is not an ℓ²-valued prior
items.statement:
Assume AC.

Let $T=\mathbb N$ and $k(i,j)=\mathbf 1_{\{i=j\}}$. The cylinder Gaussian
process with this kernel has independent $N(0,1)$ coordinates, but its
coordinate sequence is almost surely not in $\ell^2$. Thus its cylinder law
is not a tight Borel prior on $\ell^2$.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors (2008)
references.locator: Section 2.1: arbitrary-index Gaussian processes versus Borel Gaussian priors.

items.title: A rank-one finite-dimensional Gaussian process is a tight Banach prior
items.statement:
Assume AC.

Take $T=\{1,2\}$, $B=\mathbb R^2$, and $Z\sim N(0,1)$. Define
$X_1=Z$ and $X_2=2Z$. This is a singular finite Gaussian process and its
coordinate vector is a tight Borel Gaussian random element of $B$.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors (2008)
references.locator: Section 2.1: finite-dimensional distributions and Borel Gaussian priors.

references.title: A. Lunardi, M. Miranda, and D. Pallara, Infinite Dimensional Analysis
references.locator: Sections 2.2–3.1: finite-dimensional Gaussian laws and their covariance RKHS.
